newsitem.title: ITALY: Agnelli silent over who will lead Fiat.
newsitem.headline: Agnelli silent over who will lead Fiat.

text.p: The question of who will succeed Cesare Romiti as Fiat chairman will not be resolved until next year, Gianni Agnelli, honorary chairman of Italy's industrial giant, told reporters on Monday, although he himself already knows the answer.

"I know but I'm not telling you," he told reporters while attending the AGM of Agnelli family holding company IFI. But he did confirm that Paolo Cantarella would continue to be Fiat group managing director.
Romiti has said he plans to step down as chairman in June 1998 when he turns 75, in line with Fiat retirement rules.
"The question of the Fiat chairmanship is an open one and a year away," Agnelli said. "In agreement with Fiat's syndicate (of major shareholders), I've no wish to name names."

"It is important that Fiat has a young and capable MD in Paolo Cantarella. The MD always needs to have beside him a board chairman who will give him support, international experience and maintain a relationship with shareholders," Agnelli said.
Agnelli stepped down as chairman ahead of his 75th birthday in March 1996.

"The problem is who will we put alongside Cantarella who can give him this contribution. I have the solution "in pectore" (in secret), but I'm not telling you," he told reporters, requesting them not to ask him the question again for a year.
